answer: No. Your records show you were checked for a blood clot in the lung in July 2025, and it was ruled out. On 8 July 2025 you had a D-dimer blood test that was raised (0.92, where up to 0.49 is normal). A raised D-dimer is not specific, so it led to a CT scan of the chest with contrast dye (a CT angiogram) the same day. The scan report says there was no pulmonary embolism, your lungs were clear, and there was no fluid around the lungs or heart. It also noted mild wear-and-tear changes in the spine of your upper back. Your condition list has pulmonary embolism marked as 'ruled out', and a chest wall pain problem from the same day that settled by 22 July 2025. I found no later record of a clot in the lung.
short: CT angiogram of the chest on 2025-07-08 showed no pulmonary embolism (D-dimer 0.92 was raised); pulmonary embolism is recorded as ruled out. Chest wall pain from that time resolved by 2025-07-22.
